newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPC repositions in S.Korea through Sungwoo.
newsitem.headline: IPC repositions in S.Korea through Sungwoo.

text.p: IPC Corp said on Tuesday its sale of 66 million new shares or a six percent stake to South Korea's Sungwoo group would help it reposition its business in the country.
"Due to the publicity of IPC Korea...it is important for IPC to regain exposure in Korea, to reposition ourselves in the Korean market," Patrick Ngiam, chairman of IPC told reporters at a briefing.
"We would like to reestablish our position in Korea in a firmer way and therefore we need a strong partner," said Ngiam.

IPC said on Tuesday it had filed a police complaint against two directors in its unit, IPC Corporation (Korea) Ltd, for suspected wrong doings following investigations into the unit for defaulting on 570 million won of promissory notes.
IPC announced it was selling a six percent stake to Sungwoo for Singapore $39.6 million.

IPC's share sale to Sungwoo is conditional upon the approval of the Stock Exchange of Singapore for the listing and quotation of the shares. The proceeds would be used to finance IPC's investments in telecommunications businesses.
In addition, Sungwoo would manufacture Germany's Hagenuk Telecom GmbH cellular phones in Korea. IPC has a 29-percent stake in Hagenuk, which makes telecommunications equipment.
Sungwoo would distribute Hagenuk's telecommunications equipment, IPC's products and source components in South Korea for the IPC group.
Sungwoo Group comprises 10 companies including Hyundai Cement Co Ltd.
Sungwoo would build a plant in Korea at a cost of about 13 million German marks to produce Hagenuk's cellular phones, said Sung Jin Kim, director of Sungwoo Electronics Co Ltd.
The plant would be completed in the third to fourth quarter this year and would have capacity to produce 500,000 cellular phones a year, said Kim.
Ngiam said Sungwoo would start distributing Hagenuk's telecommunications products in South Korea also in the same period.
Kim said this was Sungwoo's first foray into the telecommunciations euqipment distribution business.
